bytes_note: the listing's size column is human-readable ("19.1 MiB"); the probe measures exact bytes
dataset: CHIRPS v3.0 pentad precipitation, global 0.05 degrees (GeoTIFF)

grid.coordinates: lon = x0 + (col + 0.5) * dx, lat = y0 + (row + 0.5) * dy with dy NEGATIVE; x0/y0 are the grid's WEST and NORTH edges, so this is exactly the source GeoTIFF's affine transform
grid.extent_note: [west, south, east, north] in degrees; land only
grid.no_tile_corners: a plain geographic grid: the affine rule above IS the lat/lon of every pixel and every tile corner, so no corner table is stored
grid.row_order: row 0 is the NORTHERNMOST row, 60 N (the source GeoTIFF's own order, transform (0.05, 0, -180; 0, -0.05, 60), read off the real chirps-v3.0.2019.06.1.tif). The YEARLY NETCDF copies of the same pentads run the other way (latitude ascending, -59.975 .. 59.975); this store keeps the GeoTIFF order
grid.source_variable: the GeoTIFF's single float32 band, mm/pentad, -9999 for not-land

qc_policy: the source's only flag is its fill value: _FillValue and missing_value are both -9999 and mark every pixel outside the land mask, which becomes NaN. A finite value outside [0, 5000] mm becomes NaN and is counted (`out_of_bounds`), never clipped -- the wettest five days ever recorded anywhere is about 4,900 mm, so the bound is one a measurement should not reach and a corrupt file will. No per-pixel gauge count or uncertainty is published with the pentad fields
title: Pentad precipitation, CHIRPS v3.0, 0.05 degrees, land 60 S - 60 N (exception E4: six pentads a month on a frame_table)
